description: Core rich stderr logging for the MCP gateway — ANSI color helpers, startup banner, per-scan logging with counters and timing, and scan stats tracking. This is the main deliverable: making the firewall visible. Independent of nothing — FEAT-002 depends on this.
steps: 1. Create src/gateway/colors.ts — pure ANSI color helpers, zero npm deps. Export functions: red(s), green(s), yellow(s), dim(s), bold(s), cyan(s). Each wraps string in ANSI escape codes. At module top, detect whether colors should be enabled: `const enabled = !!(process.stderr.isTTY && !process.env.NO_COLOR)`. When disabled, every function returns its input unchanged. Also export a `rule()` function that returns a line of ━ characters (the unicode box-drawing heavy horizontal U+2501, 60 chars wide). Also export `emoji` object with shield:'🛡', check:'✅', block:'🚫', warn:'⚠️', spark:'✨' — these always render regardless of TTY since they are unicode not ANSI.

2. Create a module-level scan stats tracker in src/gateway/index.ts. Add at module scope: `const stats = { totalScans: 0, allowed: 0, blocked: 0, spotlighted: 0, latencyMs: [] as number[], attackTypes: new Set<string>() }`. Export a `getGatewayStats()` function that returns a snapshot: `{ totalScans, allowed, blocked, spotlighted, attackTypes: [...stats.attackTypes], avgLatencyMs: stats.latencyMs.length ? Math.round(stats.latencyMs.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/stats.latencyMs.length) : 0 }`. This is the accessor that mcp.ts shutdown handler will call.

3. Add a `quiet` option to startGateway. Change the GatewayConfig type in src/gateway/config.ts to add an optional `quiet?: boolean` field. In startGateway(config) in index.ts, read `const quiet = config.quiet ?? (process.env.WARDEN_QUIET === '1')`. Store in a module-level `let isQuiet = false` that startGateway sets. The quiet flag suppresses per-scan ALLOW lines but NOT blocks, startup banner, or errors.

4. Replace the existing `const log = (...args) => console.error(...)` in src/gateway/index.ts with a new rich logging system. Import from './colors.ts'. Create helper functions at module level: (a) `logScan(scanNum: number, toolName: string, args: string, action: Action, riskScore: number, findings: Finding[], elapsedMs: number)` — formats and writes ONE scan line to stderr. Format: `🛡 [warden] Scan #N: toolName(args) → ✅ ALLOW (risk 0.00) 45ms` for allows (green ✅ ALLOW), `🛡 [warden] Scan #N: toolName(args) → 🚫 BLOCK (indirect_injection, 0.92) 23ms` for blocks (red 🚫 BLOCK) with a second indented line `  Reason: <first finding reason>` and third line `  Content replaced with safety message.`, `🛡 [warden] Scan #N: ... → ⚠️ SPOTLIGHT (risk 0.18) 30ms` (yellow) with indented `  Passed with data boundary wrapper.`. For ALLOW lines, skip output if isQuiet is true. For BLOCK/QUARANTINE/HUMAN_REVIEW, always print regardless of quiet. (b) `logToolVet(toolName: string, action: Action, riskScore: number, findings: Finding[], elapsedMs: number)` — formats tool-description scan at registration time. Format: `🛡 [warden] Tool "fetch" — ✅ CLEAN (0ms)` for allows, `🛡 [warden] Tool "evil_tool" — 🚫 BLOCKED (instruction_override, 0.95) 23ms` for blocks with indented reason. (c) `logStartup(...)` — see step 5. All output via console.error.

5. Implement the startup banner in startGateway(). After upstreams are connected and tools are vetted, print the banner block. Use rule() for top/bottom borders. Format:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🛡  WARDEN — AI Agent Firewall
   Scanning: tool descriptions + tool results
   API: <WARDEN_URL value>
   Upstreams: <name> (<N> tools), <name> (<N> tools)
   Exposed tools: tool1, tool2, tool3
   Mode: <verbose|quiet>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
The title line should use bold(). 'API:' value should use cyan(). Tool names in exposed list should use dim(). Replace the old `log('ready — exposing ...')` with this banner.

6. Update vetToolDescriptions() in index.ts: wrap each scanContent() call with timing (const t0 = performance.now(); ... const elapsed = performance.now() - t0). Call logToolVet() with the result. For whitelisted tools that skip scanning, call logToolVet with action 'ALLOW', riskScore 0, empty findings, 0ms. Replace the existing log('WITHHELD ...') and log('flagged ...') calls with the new logToolVet output. Increment stats.totalScans for each tool scanned (not whitelisted ones).

7. Update the CallToolRequestSchema handler in startGateway() to add rich per-scan logging. Wrap the scanContent() call with timing: `const t0 = performance.now()` before, `const elapsedMs = Math.round(performance.now() - t0)` after. Increment stats.totalScans. Based on verdict.action, increment stats.allowed/blocked/spotlighted and add finding attackTypes to stats.attackTypes. Push elapsedMs to stats.latencyMs. Build an args summary string from req.params.arguments (truncate to ~60 chars). Call logScan(stats.totalScans, toolName, argsSummary, verdict.action, verdict.riskScore, verdict.findings, elapsedMs). Replace the existing log(`${verdict.action} ${toolName} result ...`) with this. For the no-text early return (empty result), log a brief line: `🛡 [warden] Scan #N: toolName(args) → (empty result, skipped)`.

8. Write tests in tests/gateway-logging.test.ts. Test the colors.ts module: (a) with NO_COLOR=1 set, color functions return input unchanged. (b) rule() returns a string of 60 chars. Test getGatewayStats() returns the expected shape. Use `import { red, green, yellow, dim, bold, rule } from '../src/gateway/colors.ts'` and `import { getGatewayStats } from '../src/gateway/index.ts'`. Since these are pure functions, they are safe to test in bun:test without ONNX issues.
acceptance_criteria: src/gateway/colors.ts exists with red/green/yellow/dim/bold/cyan/rule exports, no npm deps
Colors auto-disable when process.stderr.isTTY is falsy or NO_COLOR is set
Every scanContent() call in index.ts is wrapped with timing measurement
A module-level scan counter increments for every scan and is shown in log lines
getGatewayStats() is exported from index.ts and returns totalScans/allowed/blocked/spotlighted/attackTypes/avgLatencyMs
Startup banner prints with rule lines, title, API URL, upstream list, exposed tools
Per-scan log lines show scan number, tool name, action with emoji, risk score, and elapsed ms
BLOCK/QUARANTINE lines always print even in quiet mode; ALLOW lines suppressed in quiet mode
All existing log() calls in index.ts are replaced — no raw log() calls remain
All output goes to stderr via console.error, never stdout
Running `bun test` passes all existing and new tests
verification: bun test — all tests pass including new tests/gateway-logging.test.ts
findings: colors.ts exports: red, green, yellow, dim, bold, cyan, rule, emoji. index.ts exports: getGatewayStats (returns { totalScans, allowed, blocked, spotlighted, attackTypes: string[], avgLatencyMs }). GatewayConfig in config.ts has optional quiet?: boolean field. The isQuiet module-level flag is set in startGateway(). CLI (src/cli.ts) does not yet expose --quiet — FEAT-002 should add that flag and pass it through to config.quiet. The shutdown handler in mcp.ts can import getGatewayStats from './gateway/index.ts' to print a summary on SIGTERM/SIGINT.
